# Conjunctions

## Conjunctions that join two phrases

A conjunction without a comma before it often joins two parts of one phrase,
so a long line breaks at a clause boundary rather than in front of it.

The formatter reads the first input and the first output root of every project in the workspace,
then writes one report for all of them.

Pass either the configuration file or the environment variable that names it
when the tool starts, otherwise the defaults in the home directory apply.

The tool is small but powerful enough to rewrite every comment in a large repository in seconds,
although the first run has to build its cache.

Neither the cache nor the lock file is ever committed to the repository by the release job,
because both of them are rebuilt on every agent.

## Conjunctions that close a list

A list of single words reads as one unit, so a line never breaks between two of its items.

The release job builds packages for every supported platform of the project,
including Linux, macOS, Windows, and FreeBSD, before it uploads them.

The formatter accepts a configuration file written in any of the supported formats,
such as TOML, YAML, JSON, or INI, from the project root.

The cleanup job never removes the directories that hold user data,
neither logs, caches, uploads, nor backups, even when the disk runs full.
